in_latin.name: Stanisław
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Slavicum, significans victoriam gloriae, ab Sclavis orientalibus origine, in terris Poloniae et Ruthenia habitatis. In Polonia, nomen Stanisław est commune, sed in Ruthenia, nomen Stanislavus est usitatum. Nomen hunc derivavimus ex lingua Polonica, quae Slavia Orientalis est, et ex lingua Ruthenica, quae Slavia Orientalis est. Nomen hunc significat victoriam gloriae et potestatem, et est nomen virtus et fortitudo. In ecclesia Catholica Romana, nomen Stanisław est nomen sanctitatis, et est nomen martyr et confessio

in_english.long_meaning: Stanisław is a Slavic name of Polish origin, meaning glory of victory and fame. It is derived from the Polish language, which is a Slavic language, and from the Ruthenian language, which is a Slavic language. The name signifies victory and fame, and is associated with virtue and strength. In the Roman Catholic Church, Stanisław is a name of sanctity, and is associated with martyrdom and confession. The name has been borne by several saints, including Saint Stanisław of Cracow, a 13th-century bishop and martyr. The name is also associated with the Polish word 'stan', meaning 'standing' or 'standing firm', and the suffix '-isław', meaning 'glory' or 'fame'. The name is commonly found in Poland and other Slavic countries, and is often given to boys born into families of Polish or Slavic descent. The name is also associated with the idea of standing firm in one's faith and convictions, and is often given to boys born into families of strong Christian faith

data.cultural_impact: Stanisław is a distinctly Polish name, spoken with pride and warmth by generations of families who have carried this name as their own. Developed from the Slavic "stan," which means "standing" or "settled," the name Stanisław has come to symbolize stability, courage, and resilience in Polish heritage. This name has stood the test of time as a testament to the enduring spirit of the Polish people. Stanisław holds a special significance in Polish history, particularly during the Middle Ages when the nation was frequently subjected to external invasions and political turmoil. The name Stanisław emerged as a source of strength and unity, giving families a steadfast identity when the world around them was in flux.
data.spiritual_significance: Beyond its cultural significance, the name Stanisław holds profound spiritual meaning as the name of several notable Catholic saints. Among them is St. Stanislaus of Szczepanów, who stood up against secular power to defend the sanctity of the Eucharist and the value of human life. Born around 1030, Stanisław served as the archbishop of Krakow, Poland. He became a champion for the people, refusing to compromise the faith or yield to political pressure. When confronted by King Bolesław II, the father of one of his priests' mistresses, Stanisław refused to grant the king a divorce. Instead, he excommunicated the king, who, in retaliation, ordered his assassination. However, in his final moments, Stanisław stood firm, embracing his impending death with forgiveness and courage. His unwavering devotion to Christ ultimately led to his canonization as a saint in 1253. To Polish Catholics, St. Stanisław represents the virtue of martyrdom, the courage to stand up against injustice, and the faithfulness to God's Word.
